# gatling-playwright-plugin

> A Gatling plugin (`io.github.i-nahornyi:gatling-playwright-plugin`) that adds Playwright-driven
> browser actions to Gatling load-test scenarios — open a URL, run a scripted Playwright flow, clean up
> the browser context — and reports page-level UI metrics (TTFB, LCP, CLS, INP, FCP) alongside Gatling's
> normal stats. One real Playwright browser per virtual user. Compatible with Gatling 3.12.0; other
> Gatling versions aren't guaranteed to work. Requires Java 17.

This file is a self-contained reference for an AI assistant writing Gatling simulations against this
plugin's public DSL — it inlines the full API surface (both Java and Scala) in one place instead of
linking out. For narrower topic pages, the canonical docs live under `docs/` in this repo:
`docs/README.md` (install), `docs/java/Api.md` / `docs/scala/Api.md` (DSL overview with links to one
page per action), `docs/WebVitals.md` (UI metrics).

## Install

Maven:
```xml
<dependency>
    <groupId>io.github.i-nahornyi</groupId>
    <artifactId>gatling-playwright-plugin</artifactId>
    <version>0.1.5</version>
</dependency>
```
Gradle: `gatling group: 'io.github.i-nahornyi', name: 'gatling-playwright-plugin', version: '0.1.5'`
(check Maven Central for the latest version). Entry points: `io.gatling.custom.browser.javaapi.BrowserDsl`
(Java, static methods) and `io.gatling.custom.browser.Predef._` (Scala, import then use top-level names).

## Mental model

- One Playwright `Browser`/`BrowserContext`/`Page` per Gatling virtual user, kept alive across actions
  in that user's scenario (not recreated per action). It self-heals if the browser/page/context gets
  closed (crash, or your own code closing it) — the next action on that user transparently relaunches.
- `open` and `executeFlow` are tracked as normal Gatling requests (show up in stats/reports);
  `browserSessionFunction` is not tracked, for page manipulation you don't want counted as a step.
- A failed `open`/`executeFlow` marks the Gatling session failed (like `exitHereIfFailed` territory)
  unless you catch the failure yourself inside `executeFlow` via `BrowserSession.setStatusKO`.
- No plugin-level timeout exists or is planned — `open`/`executeFlow` are bounded only by whatever
  timeout the Playwright call itself uses (30s default, or `.withDefaultTimeout(millis)` on the
  protocol, or a per-call `NavigateOptions`/`ClickOptions().setTimeout(...)`). Never pass
  `setTimeout(0)` in a load test. See "Timeouts" below.
- Inside `executeFlow`/`browserSessionFunction`, don't fan out your own concurrency against `page` (one
  actor owns one `Page`, so work for a given virtual user is inherently sequential) and don't block with
  anything that isn't a timeout-aware Playwright call (your own infinite loop or blocking I/O can hang
  that virtual user forever — nothing in the plugin can bound that).

## Browser Protocol setup

Java:
```java
import io.gatling.custom.browser.javaapi.BrowserDsl;
import io.gatling.javaapi.core.ProtocolBuilder;

ProtocolBuilder browserProtocol = BrowserDsl
        .gatlingBrowser()
        // Optional setup block
        .withLaunchOptions(new LaunchOptions().setHeadless(false))
        .withContextOptions(new NewContextOptions().setViewportSize(1920, 1080).setIsMobile(true))
        .enableUIMetrics()
        .withDefaultTimeout(15000);

setUp(mainScenario.injectOpen(atOnceUsers(1))).protocols(browserProtocol);
```

Scala:
```scala
import io.gatling.custom.browser.Predef._

val browserProtocol: Protocol = gatlingBrowser
    //// This part of setup block is optional
    .withContextOptions(new NewContextOptions().setViewportSize(1920, 1080))
    .withLaunchOptions(new LaunchOptions().setHeadless(false))
    .enableUIMetrics()
    .withDefaultTimeout(15000)
    ////

setUp(mainScenario.inject(atOnceUsers(1))).protocols(browserProtocol)
```

Builder methods (both languages, chainable, all optional):
- `withLaunchOptions(LaunchOptions)` — Playwright `BrowserType.LaunchOptions` (e.g. `setHeadless`).
- `withContextOptions(NewContextOptions)` — Playwright `Browser.NewContextOptions` (e.g.
  `setViewportSize`, `setIsMobile`).
- `enableUIMetrics()` — turn on web-vitals collection for `open` actions, see "UI metrics" below.
- `withDefaultTimeout(millis)` — forwards to Playwright's own
  `BrowserContext.setDefaultTimeout`/`setDefaultNavigationTimeout` on every context the plugin creates,
  so you don't have to repeat `NavigateOptions.setTimeout(...)` on every `open()` call.


## Action name

Every action takes a name (shown in Gatling stats), which can be a literal, a Gatling EL string, or a
function of the session:

Java: `BrowserDsl.browserAction("HomePage")` / `BrowserDsl.browserAction("#{actionName}")` /
`BrowserDsl.browserAction(session -> session.getString("actionName"))`

Scala: `browserAction("HomePage")` / `browserAction("#{actionName}")` /
`browserAction(session => session("actionName").as[String])`

## Actions

| Action | Tracked in reports? | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `open` | yes | Navigate to a URL |
| `executeFlow` | yes | Run an arbitrary scripted Playwright flow against `page` |
| `browserSessionFunction` | no | Manipulate the page/session without tracking a step |
| `browserCleanContext` | n/a | Close and recreate the Playwright `BrowserContext` (e.g. end of a loop) |

### Open

Java:
```java
BrowserDsl.browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/");                 // static URL
BrowserDsl.browserAction("name").open("#{url}");                                    // EL string
BrowserDsl.browserAction("name").open(session -> session.getString("url"));         // function

// Optional: Playwright NavigateOptions
BrowserDsl.browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/")
        .withNavigateOptions(new Page.NavigateOptions().setWaitUntil(LOAD));

// Optional: load validation — a custom JS "is the page ready" expression, polled via page.waitForFunction
PageLoadValidator v = new PageLoadValidator(validationScriptJs, null,
        new Page.WaitForFunctionOptions().setPollingInterval(100).setTimeout(30000));
BrowserDsl.browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/").withLoadValidations(v);

// Optional: load validation using the plugin's built-in "resource inactivity" default script
BrowserDsl.browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/").withLoadValidations();
```

Scala:
```scala
browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/")
browserAction("name").open("#{url}")
browserAction("name").open(session => session("url").as[String])

browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/").withNavigateOptions(new Page.NavigateOptions().setWaitUntil(LOAD))

val v = PageLoadValidator(validationScriptJs, null, new Page.WaitForFunctionOptions().setPollingInterval(100).setTimeout(30000))
browserAction("name").open("https://gatling.io/").withLoadValidations(v)

browserAction("name").open("https://docs.gatling.io/").withLoadValidations()
```

### Flow (`executeFlow`)

Runs a `(Page, BrowserSession) -> BrowserSession` callback. **Always return `browserSession`** (or the
result of `browserSession.updateBrowserSession(...)` if you changed anything) — nothing is persisted
otherwise, same rule as returning a new `Session` from a plain Gatling `exec`.

Java:
```java
BrowserDsl.browserAction("test").executeFlow((page, browserSession) -> {
    page.navigate("https://docs.gatling.io/");
    page.locator("//*[@id=\"ai-initial-message\"]").isVisible();
    return browserSession;
});
```

Scala:
```scala
browserAction("test").executeFlow((page, browserSession) => {
    page.navigate("https://docs.gatling.io/")
    page.locator("//*[@id=\"ai-initial-message\"]").isVisible()
    browserSession
})
```

Reading/writing the Gatling session inside the callback (Java):
```java
Boolean valueFromSession = (Boolean) browserSession.resolveSessionValue("#{url.exists()}");
String another = browserSession.resolveSessionValue(s -> s.getString("url") + "updated").toString();
Session session = browserSession.getGatlingSession().set("your_args", page.title());
return browserSession.updateBrowserSession(session);
```
Scala:
```scala
val valueFromSession = browserSession.resolveSessionValue("#{url.exists()}")
val modified = browserSession.resolveSessionValue(session => s"${session("url").as[String]}updated")
val session: Session = browserSession.getGatlingSession.set("your_args", page.title())
browserSession.updateBrowserSession(session)
```

Overriding reported action timing (e.g. from `page.evaluate("performance.timing")`) — Java:
```java
browserSession.setActionStartTime(timing.get("navigationStart").longValue());
browserSession.setActionEndTime(timing.get("loadEventEnd").longValue());
```
Scala:
```scala
browserSession.setActionStartTime(timing("navigationStart").asInstanceOf[Long])
browserSession.setActionEndTime(timing("loadEventEnd").asInstanceOf[Long])
```

Handling an assertion/error and marking KO yourself (Java):
```java
try {
    PlaywrightAssertions.assertThat(page).hasTitle("expected");
} catch (AssertionFailedError e) {
    browserSession.setStatusKO("custom failure reason");
}
return browserSession;
```
Scala:
```scala
try {
  PlaywrightAssertions.assertThat(page).hasTitle("expected")
} catch {
  case _: AssertionFailedError => browserSession.setStatusKO("custom failure reason")
}
browserSession
```
Important: `setStatusKO(...)` does **not** stop the callback or throw — code after it still runs — and
it does not retroactively mark `browserSession.getGatlingSession().isFailed()` true either; the plugin
applies that to the Gatling session only *after* the callback returns. To bail out of the rest of the
callback, use a plain early `return`. To skip risky work in a *later* action once an earlier one already
failed, check `getGatlingSession().isFailed()` at the top of that later `executeFlow`.

### Browser Session Function

Like `executeFlow`, but not tracked as a Gatling request — for extracting data / manipulating the page
without counting it as a step.

Java: `BrowserDsl.browserSessionFunction((page, browserSession) -> { Session s = browserSession.getGatlingSession().set("pageTitle", page.title()); return browserSession.updateBrowserSession(s); });`

Scala: `browserSessionFunction((page, browserSession) => { val s = browserSession.getGatlingSession.set("pageTitle", page.title()); browserSession.updateBrowserSession(s) })`

### Clean Context

Closes and recreates the Playwright `BrowserContext` for the current virtual user — typically at the
end of a loop iteration, to start the next iteration with a clean context.

Java: `BrowserDsl.browserCleanContext()`  ·  Scala: `browserCleanContext()`

## BrowserSession reference

Passed into `executeFlow`/`browserSessionFunction`. Wraps the Gatling `Session` immutably — like
Gatling's own `Session`, no method mutates in place; always capture and return the result of
`updateBrowserSession(...)` to persist a change.

| Concern | Java | Scala | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Read session | `getGatlingSession()` → `Session` | `getGatlingSession` → `Session` | read-only |
| Read one attribute | — | `getGatlingSession(name: String)` → `SessionAttribute` | Scala only |
| Persist a change | `updateBrowserSession(Session)` → `BrowserSession` | same | **must return this** |
| Resolve EL expr | `resolveSessionValue(String)` → `Object` | `resolveSessionValue(String)` → `Any` | e.g. `"#{url}"` |
| Resolve via function | `resolveSessionValue(Function<Session,Object>)` | `resolveSessionValue(Expression[Any])` | |
| Set start time (now) | `setActionStartTime()` | same | |
| Set start time (explicit) | `setActionStartTime(long)` | `setActionStartTime(Long)` | epoch millis |
| Get start time | `getActionStartTime()` → `long` | `getActionStartTime` → `Long` | `0` if never set |
| Set end time (now) | `setActionEndTime()` | same | |
| Set end time (explicit) | `setActionEndTime(long)` | `setActionEndTime(Long)` | epoch millis |
| Get end time | `getActionEndTime()` → `long` | `getActionEndTime` → `Long` | `0` if never set |
| Mark OK | `setStatusOK()` | same | |
| Mark KO | `setStatusKO()` / `setStatusKO(String)` | same | |
| Get status | `getStatus()` | `getStatus` | `Status` OK/KO |
| Get error message | `getErrorMessage()` → `Optional`-like Scala `Option<String>` (check `.isDefined()` then `.get()`) | `getErrorMessage` → `Option[String]` | |

## Timeouts

There is no plugin-level timeout and none is planned — a stuck `open`/`executeFlow` is bounded only by
whatever timeout the underlying Playwright call uses, exactly like plain Playwright:

- Protocol-wide default: `.withDefaultTimeout(millis)` on the protocol builder (see above) — applies to
  every context the plugin creates.
- Per-`open()` override: `.withNavigateOptions(new Page.NavigateOptions().setTimeout(5000))` — wins over
  the protocol default for that one call.
- Per-call override inside `executeFlow`: pass `*Options().setTimeout(...)` on the individual Playwright
  call (`page.locator(...).click(new Locator.ClickOptions().setTimeout(5000))`), same as plain Playwright.

A navigation/call that exceeds its timeout throws Playwright's own `TimeoutError`, which the plugin
reports as a clean KO on that action — it does not hang the virtual user. **Never pass `setTimeout(0)`**
in a load test (it disables the safety net), and never block inside `executeFlow`/
`browserSessionFunction` with anything that isn't a timeout-aware Playwright call.

## UI metrics (web vitals)

Enable with `.enableUIMetrics()` on the protocol builder. Collected only for `open` actions: FCP, LCP,
CLS, INP, TTFB. Written as CSV (`MetricType,timestamp,actionName,status,metricName,value`, e.g.
`WEB_VITALS,1757624157101,homePage,OK,FCP,1042`) to `ui_metrics.csv` in the current Gatling run's results
directory (`target/gatling/<run>/` for Maven, `reports/gatling/<run>/` for Gradle) — read it alongside
the normal Gatling HTML report.
